subject.title: [Bug]: Windows gateway listens but local health/status time out after Telegram polling stall (v2026.5.20)

question: Should unrecovered Telegram/channel stalls escalate to supervised Gateway process recovery, or should recovery remain inside Telegram/channel/session layers until current-main affected-host proof identifies the exact blocker?
rationale: Current code intentionally caps channel restarts without exiting, while the reported failure is process-level unresponsiveness; changing that boundary affects operator behavior, active sessions, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-main affected-host proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

options.title: Define Supervised Recovery
options.body: Implement a bounded Gateway watchdog or process-exit policy for unrecovered stalls with upgrade notes and Windows proof.

options.title: Stay Channel-Scoped
options.body: Continue fixing only narrower Telegram transport/session bugs and avoid process-level recovery unless a fresh repro proves it is necessary.

recommendation.title: Reproduce First, Then Choose Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-main affected-host proof, and decide process-level recovery only if channel/session fixes still leave Gateway probes timing out.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the Telegram polling isolation work and already attempted the targeted real Telegram reproduction that frames the remaining proof gap.
